solutions.check: 33 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Cut the woman's slinky move!

parts.note: a slit is a cut
the woman's thing is hers: HER

explanation.surface: A woman's sinuous dance step gets snipped out of the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cut" looks like an order to remove something, but it is simply the first noun of the build.
explanation.definitionFit: A slither is a smooth, sliding, snake-like movement, which is exactly a slinky move.

clue.text: Start to screw royal to cut the ice, so to speak

definitions.text: cut the ice, so to speak

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of screw
Kate, Princess of Wales, is a royal

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion about a member of the royal family, dressed up as breaking the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Private Eye tone makes "screw royal" look like the sense, but only its S is used; "so to speak" flags that skating literally cuts ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater's blades carve lines in the ice, so to skate is, jokily, to cut the ice.

clue.text: One resistance soldier not giving a shit routinely?

parts.note: Roman numeral one
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a regular is a soldier in the standing army

explanation.surface: A member of the resistance who is constipated, or who just doesn't care about routine.
explanation.walkthrough: An irregular is also a guerrilla fighter, so the surface's resistance soldier is the answer too; the question mark admits the lavatory joke in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not go to the toilet on a regular schedule is, in the medical sense, irregular.

clue.text: Bit of thigh and rest's disturbed, pet?

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
REST rearranged; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pet has been sleeping badly on their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as is: rest is disturbed. HAM for the back of the thigh is the root of hamstring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent kept as a pet.

clue.text: Bishop's dropped from office — source of beef?

indicators.note: something dropped from a word is taken out of it

parts.note: a local branch is an office of a bank or firm
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop leaves his office and someone asks what the grievance was about.
explanation.walkthrough: "Beef" hints at a complaint; the question mark says it is the cattle kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch raises beef cattle, so it is where beef comes from.

clue.text: Goodness comes from a lot of money, money initially lacking

parts.note: G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: initially lacking says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise at a fortune appearing from nowhere, though the cash itself is missing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially lacking' strips the L from LOLLY, British slang for cash, leaving OLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Golly is a mild exclamation of surprise, like goodness me.

clue.text: Great to admit it's a big 'un

parts.note: gr. is an abbreviation for great
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to confess that something is very large.
explanation.walkthrough: "Admit" looks like a container instruction, but OWN UP simply follows GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call an adult a grown-up or a big 'un.

clue.text: Solitary unit between political extremes?

indicators.note: a piece placed between two others sits inside them

parts.note: left and right, the two ends of the political spectrum
one is the unit

explanation.surface: A lone centrist is squeezed between the far left and the far right.
explanation.walkthrough: The political extremes are the letters L and R, the left and right ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a person who lives alone: a loner.

clue.text: see 15dn.
City: "Cameron's at variance"

indicators.note: letters at variance disagree with their order

parts.note: CAMERONSAT rearranged

explanation.surface: A headline quoting David Cameron as being at odds with a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The AT of "at variance" is part of the letters; only "variance" instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is a city, the state capital of California.

clue.text: see 28dn.
Crew relieving wife from burden

indicators.note: to relieve a burden of something is to take it off
says which word loses the letter

parts.note: a weight is a burden
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A household crew takes the load off the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is the crew of eight oarsmen, so "Crew" is the definition, not a group of helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is a boat and its crew of eight rowers.

clue.text: Under-performing during hot date causing division

indicators.note: letters performing are doing a turn, rearranged
one thing during another sits inside it

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
UNDER rearranged
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone who fails in bed on a hot date and the couple split up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Under-performing" reads as one word but splits into fodder and instruction. A hundred is an old subdivision of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred was an administrative division of a shire in England.

clue.text: China was the first to back capitalist newspaper

indicators.note: sent back, the word reads right to left

parts.note: whoever was first led
the Financial Times, the City's paper

explanation.surface: China is credited with being first to support a business paper.
explanation.walkthrough: "China" is the pottery, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft, a kind of china.

clue.text: NRA could after shifting pot

indicators.note: the letters as they stand after being shifted about

parts.note: NRACOULD rearranged

explanation.surface: The US gun lobby wonders what it might do after moving marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pot" suggests cannabis in a surface about American politics; it is the cooking kind. The NRA is the National Rifle Association.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cauldron is the big iron pot hung over a fire, the witches' kind.

clue.text: Trick action misfired — missing a ball

indicators.note: a misfired word has its letters go off wrongly
missing means that letter is taken out

parts.note: ACTION without an O
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A sporting trick shot goes wrong and misses the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter O stands for a ball because of its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful trick or caper, usually heard as antics.

clue.text: (& 7dn.) Tony's lost the plot finally? So far, no

indicators.note: something lost is all over the place, so these letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally says take the closing letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the last letters of the and plot

explanation.surface: A jibe that a politician named Tony, presumably Blair, has at last gone mad, with a curt answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and T, the end letters of 'the plot', and 'lost' mixes them with TONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet means not up to now, which is the sense of so far, no.

clue.text: Rubbish females breaking into store

indicators.note: a burglar breaking into a place ends up inside it

parts.note: a pile is a stored heap
F for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Nonsense about women burgling a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter makes the plural, as FF for females, like pp for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the nonsense sense: calling someone's talk piffle dismisses it as rubbish.

clue.text: Ignored, in disbelief — or got tense

indicators.note: What is in a phrase sits inside it, so the answer is a run of letters within the words that follow.

parts.note: the letters run on unbroken across the words

explanation.surface: Someone hears they have been overlooked and reacts with disbelief and nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: "Got tense" looks like nervousness, and the dash makes 'or got tense' read as an afterthought; the answer runs across the last letter of 'disbelief' to the first three of 'tense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ignored has been forgotten, left out of mind.

clue.text: Having erection after can cause trouble

parts.note: can and stir are both slang for prison
something erect is up

explanation.surface: An arousal-related mishap in the loo that leads to embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: "Can" is a toilet in the surface but British prison slang in the wordplay, as is stir; "after" fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: you stir up trouble the way you stir a pot, making things churn.

clue.text: Action: corpses everywhere

indicators.note: letters everywhere are scattered all over

parts.note: CORPSES rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director's call to action on a set littered with bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: "Action" is the lawsuit sense, not the director's call.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a process is a legal action or the writ that starts one.

clue.text: Still flipping crushing virtue? Sheer recklessness!

indicators.note: flipped over, the word reads backwards
one piece crushing another holds it squeezed inside

parts.note: still and yet both mean nevertheless
merit is a virtue

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone still stamping all over decency.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the instruction to turn YET round.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is rash boldness, reckless audacity.

clue.text: Have sex, wrapping chain on top of erect chopper

indicators.note: a wrapper goes round what it holds

parts.note: animals mate
ch. is the abbreviation for chain, a surveyor's measure

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of erect

explanation.surface: A saucy line about sex, a chain and an erect chopper.
explanation.walkthrough: "Chopper" is slang for penis in the surface; the definition is the cutting tool. "On" adds E after CH inside the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife for chopping, a chopper.

clue.text: City centre's gone (Conservative cuts) — that'll do for me

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the setter: the answer will serve as a name for me, the writer of this puzzle

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: lops means cuts off

explanation.surface: A grumble that a city's heart has been ripped out by Tory austerity, which would finish the speaker off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre's gone' removes IT from CITY to leave CY. The definition 'me' is the setter speaking: Cyclops sets this Private Eye puzzle, and 'that'll do for me' means the answer will stand for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclops is the pseudonym of the Private Eye setter, so the answer refers to the clue's own author.

clue.text: Cringe about Bercow going topless

indicators.note: about says the letters turn round, the front part moving to the end
going topless says the first letter of the name is removed

parts.note: John Bercow, the former Speaker of the House of Commons; taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone shrinking in embarrassment at the image of the ex-Speaker without his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' takes the B from BERCOW to leave ERCOW, and 'about' moves its ER to the end. John Bercow was the famously theatrical Speaker of the UK House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back in fear, the same as cringe.

clue.text: Get to shag in Number ten — twice

definitions.meaning: slang for succeeding in getting sex
twenty, reached by counting ten twice

explanation.surface: A political scandal: sex at the Prime Minister's residence, twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is Downing Street, the PM's home, but here it is just the number 10, doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is slang for landing sex; a score is twenty, two tens.

clue.text: Mad — which shows there's something wrong

definitions.meaning: the mark a teacher puts beside a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Being furious is a sign that something is amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mad" is angry, not insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means angry, and a cross is the mark put next to an error.

clue.text: Technique in opening of skimpy top

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of skimpy
to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: The knack of wearing a revealing low-cut top.
explanation.walkthrough: "Top" is a garment in the surface but the slang verb for murder in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill is technique, expertise at doing something.

clue.text: Crack: "F— the police!"

parts.note: the letter left before the dash
the law is slang for the police

explanation.surface: A rude anti-police slogan, bleeped.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash does the work: only the F of the expletive survives.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a crack in china or glass is a flaw, a defect in the material.

clue.text: (& 9dn.) New 'tool' — sadly on which the finish is disappointing

definitions.text: on which the finish is disappointing

indicators.note: letters sadly placed are in a sorry order

parts.note: NEWTOOL rearranged

explanation.surface: A sex toy that fails to satisfy at the climax.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer continues into 9 across. The phrase "to end on a low note" is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending on a low note means finishing disappointingly, so a low note is what a disappointing finish ends on.

clue.text: Say Republican's constrained by rampant conceit, just like Trump

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia, means for example, which is what say means here

indicators.note: constrained by says the letter is held inside the other letters
rampant means running wild, so the letters of conceit are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a Republican trapped by his own runaway vanity, exactly like Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampant' rearranges CONCEIT to OCENTIC, and 'constrained by' puts R inside it between the T and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric means self-centred, the satirical charge laid against Trump, here offered as an example.

clue.text: Angry talk when doctor shafts pig — perverse!

indicators.note: to shaft is to penetrate, so the doctor goes inside
perverse means turned the wrong way

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A furious outburst at a vet doing something unspeakable to a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: To have words with someone is to argue, so WORDS is angry talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have words with someone is to quarrel, so the plural means angry talk.

clue.text: Going on and on about temperature, er, in back passage

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it
to go back is to go in reverse, so the passage is read from its end

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage
T for temperature
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A long, hesitant complaint about heat in the rear passage.
explanation.walkthrough: "Back passage" is a coy word for the rectum; here it is a reversed lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal goes on and on without end.
